recall.minute: Inference computes prediction = f(input features, trained model) with the model fixed, for example predict_species((5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2)) returning setosa. Feature encoding converts raw inputs into numerical vectors and must be identical in training and serving, through a shared library, to avoid training-serving skew. Four serving designs: a library (embedded call, e.g. Tesseract), a service (replicated REST server), batch processing (move the model to the data, e.g. nightly recommendations) and cached predictions (precompute and look up). Zero-downtime strategies: basic (all at once, only for tiny apps), ramped (one node at a time, Kubernetes' default, both versions coexist), blue/green (two identical environments, instant rollback, double cost, all traffic shifts at once) and canary (small subset first). MLOps handles predictive models with drift and retraining (MLflow, Kubeflow); LLMOps handles prompts, RAG, hallucinations and token costs (LangChain, LlamaIndex); AgentOps handles reasoning traces, tool authorisation, loops and human-in-the-loop (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), each with distinct quality, operational, reliability, data, efficiency and user metrics. An MLOps simulation runs data, validation, features, training, registry, deployment, monitoring and PSI-triggered retraining.
